chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he did not validate a testimony upon a testimony in a hadd (fixed punishment) case.

key_terms.شَهَادَةً عَلَى شَهَادَةٍ: Testimony upon testimony (one testimony confirming another)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on 'testimony upon testimony' in hadd cases according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted through the reliable chain of Safwan and Talhah, establishes a specific evidentiary standard for hadd punishments, distinguishing them from other civil cases. In Shia jurisprudence, this prevents the accumulation of weak or corroborative testimonies to create a stronger case, ensuring that each witness provides independent, direct knowledge of the act, thereby safeguarding against the severity of fixed punishments. This principle reflects the cautious approach (ihtiyat) taken in applying hadd, where the burden of proof is held to a high standard of clarity and independence.
